cv2|CascadeClassifier: opencv-contrib-python 5 has it at the same name, and its cv2.data folder has the haarcascade XML files (opencv-python 5.1.0.95 has neither). Or pip install "opencv-python<5".
cv2|HOGDescriptor: The same name in opencv-contrib-python 5, or pip install "opencv-python<5".
cv2|KAZE_create: cv2.xfeatures2d.KAZE_create() in opencv-contrib-python 5. cv2.ORB_create and cv2.SIFT_create stay in opencv-python.
cv2|SIFT_create: In opencv-python from 4.4.0.46 (and in the 3.4 line from 3.4.11.43). On an older install: upgrade, or cv2.xfeatures2d.SIFT_create() from opencv-contrib-python.
cv2|TrackerCSRT_create: Only ever in opencv-contrib-python (top level, every release read).
cv2|TrackerKCF_create: Only ever in opencv-contrib-python (top level, every release read).
cv2|aruco: opencv-python has cv2.aruco from 4.7.0.72 (ArucoDetector, getPredefinedDictionary). Before that, and for the old functions, install opencv-contrib-python.
cv2|barcode: opencv-python has it from 4.8.0.76, opencv-contrib-python from 4.5.3.56.
cv2|createShapeContextDistanceExtractor: Still at the same name in opencv-contrib-python.
cv2|cv2: Write import cv2. import cv2.cv2 works up to 4.5.5.64 (3.4.17.63 in the 3.4 line); from 4.6.0.66 it raises "ImportError: Bindings generation error".
cv2|estimateRigidTransform: cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D(src, dst) (what fullAffine=False did) or cv2.estimateAffine2D(src, dst) (fullAffine=True). Both return (matrix, inliers), not the matrix alone.
cv2|groupRectangles: The same name in opencv-contrib-python 5, or pip install "opencv-python<5".
cv2|haarcascades: cv2.data.haarcascades (the folder path as a string).
cv2|logPolar: cv2.warpPolar(src, dsize, center, maxRadius, cv2.WARP_POLAR_LOG); OpenCV's docstring in 4.14 says the two give the same result.
cv2|ml: cv2.ml (SVM_create, KNearest_create, ...) is in opencv-contrib-python 5, or pip install "opencv-python<5".
cv2|xfeatures2d: Only in opencv-contrib-python. For SIFT alone, cv2.SIFT_create() is in opencv-python from 4.4.0.46. cv2.xfeatures2d.SURF_create exists but raises "This algorithm is patented and is excluded in this configuration" in the PyPI wheels.
cv2.aruco|ArucoDetector: New in 4.7.0. On an older release use cv2.aruco.detectMarkers(image, dictionary, parameters=parameters) from opencv-contrib-python, or upgrade.
cv2.aruco|CharucoBoard_create: cv2.aruco.CharucoBoard((squaresX, squaresY), squareLength, markerLength, dictionary); then board.getChessboardCorners() and board.generateImage(size).
cv2.aruco|detectMarkers: cv2.aruco.ArucoDetector(dictionary, parameters).detectMarkers(image), there from 4.7.0. OpenCV's own text in 4.14: "Use class ArucoDetector::detectMarkers".
cv2.aruco|drawAxis: cv2.drawFrameAxes(image, cameraMatrix, distCoeffs, rvec, tvec, length). OpenCV's own text in 4.5.5: "use cv::drawFrameAxes".
cv2.aruco|estimatePoseSingleMarkers: OpenCV's own text in 4.14: "Use cv::solvePnP" (cv2.solvePnP, once per marker, with the marker's four corners).
cv2.dnn|DictValue: A clean install has it. This error usually means the files of two OpenCV packages are mixed: cv2/typing (shipped from 4.8.0.76) reads this name when cv2 is imported. Uninstall every OpenCV package and install one.
cv2.dnn|readNetFromCaffe: Gone with the Caffe importer: in 5.1.0, cv2.dnn.readNet on a .caffemodel raises "Caffe importer has been removed" and asks for an ONNX-converted model or an older OpenCV. cv2.dnn.readNetFromONNX is still there; or pip install "opencv-python<5".
cv2.dnn|readNetFromDarknet: Gone with the Darknet importer (5.1.0's readNet on a .weights file: "Darknet importer has been removed"). Convert the model to ONNX and use cv2.dnn.readNetFromONNX, or pip install "opencv-python<5".
cv2.dnn|readNetFromTensorflow: 5.0.0.93 still has it. In 5.1.0, cv2.dnn.readNet on a .pb raises "TensorFlow importer has been removed" and asks for an ONNX-converted model or an older OpenCV; readNetFromTFLite and readNetFromONNX are still there.
cv2.dnn|readNetFromTorch: Removed in the same release as the Caffe and Darknet readers. cv2.dnn.readNetFromONNX is still there; or pip install "opencv-python<5".
